item.title: Development of the LIMB-QOL measurement system
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Lapin, Cleveland Clinic

Jessica Roydhouse, University of Tasmania

This special collection focuses on the LIMB-QOL, a comprehensive patient-reported outcome system designed to evaluate multiple aspects of health and functioning in individuals who have experienced limb loss or severe extremity injuries. The measurement system addresses physical, emotional, and social dimensions of quality of life and was developed through a large collaborative initiative supported by the U.S. Department of Defense and based at the University of Delaware.

The collection brings together foundational papers that introduce the LIMB-QOL system to both researchers and clinical practitioners, documenting its development process and demonstrating its application in assessing outcomes for people with major extremity injuries.

item.title: Enhancing Population Health Assessment: Key Papers from the EQ-DAPHNIE Project
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Lapin, Cleveland Clinic

Jessica Roydhouse, University of Tasmania

The EQ-DAPHNIE project, funded by the EuroQol Research Foundation, conducted an extensive population health assessment across 15 countries, collecting demographic data, social determinants of health, and multiple generic and disease-specific patient-reported outcome measures. This special collection brings together research emerging from this landmark initiative that addresses various aspects of health measurement and population variation.

item.title: Patient experience data in regulatory and health technology assessment
item.content:encoded:
Wen-Hung Chen, AstraZeneca

Lori D. McLeod, RTI Health Solutions

Regulatory and health technology assessment bodies increasingly recognize the importance of incorporating patient perspectives when evaluating healthcare products. Patient experience data encompasses patient-reported outcomes, clinical outcome assessments, and patient preference information. However, these data are often inconsistently integrated and evaluated in decision-making processes.

This collection invites submissions exploring how patient experience data, including preferences, symptoms, and health-related quality of life measures, are assessed and utilized in regulatory and health technology assessment contexts. The collection welcomes original research, reviews, and discussion papers addressing recent developments in this field, as well as work on emerging applications such as artificial intelligence and digital health technologies in patient experience research.
